slides.heading: Search For Range
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Hard · Searching
slides.narration: Let's solve Search For Range, a hard searching problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: First and last index of target in a sorted array, [-1, -1] if absent.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. First and last index of target in a sorted array, -1, -1 if absent. Two modified binary searches.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Two binary searches: one biased left for the first occurrence, one biased right for the last.
slides.narration: Two binary searches: one biased left for the first occurrence, one biased right for the last.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Binary search then expand → O(n) worst
slides.narration: Scanning, or finding one match and expanding, can be linear with many duplicates. Two lower-bound searches give both ends in log n.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 3. Return both indices or minus ones
slides.narration: Step by step. First, search keeping left on matches. Second, search keeping right on matches. Third, return both indices or minus ones.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Lower bound of 45: 4
slides.narration: Binary search for the first index whose value is at least 45: index 4.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Upper end: 9
slides.narration: Search again for 46: index 10. One before it, 9, is the last 45.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: Bound returns the first index whose value is at least t. The range is bound of t through bound of t plus one minus one, if the value at the lower bound equals t.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of log n. Space is constant.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: Check the target actually exists at the lower bound.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
slides.narration: Use the lower-bound and upper-bound vocabulary.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Two binary searches: one biased left for the first occurrence, one biased right for the last.
slides.narration: To recap Search For Range: Two binary searches: one biased left for the first occurrence, one biased right for the last. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
